exact_statement: For disjoint uniform physical Boolean blocks F=g(f_1,...,f_k), let a_i=E(D_i g)^2 and gamma_ij be the probability, over other induced outputs, that the i,j gate face has corner product -1. With Q(f)=2^(1-n)N_odd(f), Q(F)=sum_i a_i Q(f_i)+(1/2)sum_{i<j}gamma_ij I(f_i)I(f_j). A query x in child h of F=A+B h has q_x(F)=t q_x(h)+(Inf_x(h)/2)I(1-2B^2), t=E B^2. For the explicit five-bit bent/point-flip selector c of DERIVATION.md, d=1/16,m=3/16,I(c)=37/16 and B_s(c)-Lbin(m,d)>1/4; hence its queried selector remains K=4 bad in every nontrivial disjoint outer composition. For F_LN=1-(1+P_N)(1-product_{j=1}^L c_j)/2, L,N>=1, I=[37L/16+(1-(3/16)^L)N]/2. A complete selectors-first tree spends at least L(4+N)/32 bad odd-face credit; for N=L^2 its ratio to I is at least L/53. A complete parity-first tree spends exactly L/8, ratio at most 4/37. The selectors-first signed mean residual bank is between zero and L(2L+4)16^(-(L+1)); it contains beta^2 log(1/M^2)/2+O(beta^2) at beta=-M/3. Thus at fixed K=4 every-tree O(I) credit is false, while this family satisfies a some-tree bound and has H/I tending to zero when N=L^2. No universal some-tree bound is asserted. Extension at version 2: for arbitrary disjoint Boolean controller w and untouched Boolean core h, F=1-(1-w)(1-h)/2, r=Pr(h=-1),t=Pr(w=-1),a=Ew and beta=(Ew_0-Ew_1)/2, a controller query has d_F=r d_w, q_F=r q_w+(I(h)/2)d_w and B_F=r B_w+R_r(a,beta), where R_r=L(1-r+r a,r beta)+r(1-r)L(1-a,beta)-r L(a,beta). For any complete controller tree and its LIFTED K4-bad set E, its bad prefix bill is r sum_E p_v q_w+(I(h)/2)sum_E p_v d_w. Its actual terminals retain t H(h),t I(h),t Q(h). Let w=-G_L,h=G_M with the fixed five-bit modules above. The controller selectors-first tree individually costs exactly (4/37)I(w), as does the core selectors-first tree. Nevertheless its lifted prefix bill is at least r L/4+(37/16)LM/32. For M=L, I(F)=37L/16 and the prefix ratio is at least L/32+4r/37, unbounded. Its total signed selector mean residual is between zero and L(2L+4)16^(-(L+1)). This refutes transferring arbitrary already-paid K4 controller trees solely from their own bad-face bill. H(F_LL)/I(F_LL)<=160/37. At K7, every complete controller-first tree in this fixed-module family has ZERO bad credit for all L,M>=1, certified by 13^13*499^499>2^4517 and physical influence granularity. No all-parameter K4 data-first assertion, universal policy or FEI proof is claimed.

exact_statement: Let S,W,U,V be independent compatible point indicators on disjoint uniform blocks of positive widths s,L,R,T, and let g be an independent balanced Boolean sign. Set F=1+[WUV OR S(U OR V)](g-1), q=2^-R,r=2^-T,eta=2^-(L+R+T),e=q+r-qr-eta,alpha=2^-s,JB=(L+R+T)eta,JC=R q(1-r)+T r(1-q),JD=JB+JC,pi=eta+alpha e. Query S until failure or completion, then resolve WUV or U OR V and stop at a constant or the actual g. For e<=1/8 every live separator query has B_i/Inf_i<1781/480<4. In particular min(R,T)>=4 gives zero localized strict-K4 bad-control-prefix bill for every s,L. Otherwise define m_*=ceil(log2(min(R,T)+2))+2<=5; in the rare regime define m_*=0. The reserve at live layer j is W_j=2^-j[M_j JD+e M_j(M_j-1)/2+M_j e I(g)], M_j=min(j,m_*), and is zero after separator failure. Its physical drift equals the actual child-product face price c_j=2^-j[JD+(j-1)e+e I(g)] at j<=m_* and zero otherwise. Every possible bad-layer debit is bounded by this drift. With I_sep=s alpha e,I_other=(1-alpha)JB+alpha JC,I_terminal=pi I(g), the entire controller-prefix bad bill obeys Q_bad<=W_s<=5 I_other+2 I_sep+5 I_terminal<=5 I(F), uniformly in all widths and core dimension. Terminal entropy remains pi H(g). Moreover H(F)<=(4+2/ln2)(I_sep+I_other)+W_s+pi H(g); with a separately proved terminal rate C0, H(F)<=max(9+2/ln2,C0+5)I(F). No prescribed-witness funding, arbitrary unbalanced-core K4 bound or general nested-selector reserve is asserted.
